body:
Maintainer's decision (2026-09-19), landing with the housekeeping sweep T-218.

1. Tombstone retention 90 -> 45 days (gc.RETENTION_MS). The window exists so a device that was
   offline can still catch up incrementally: past it, its cursor falls below meta.gc_horizon and it
   gets 410 full_resync_required, which both clients handle by pushing their dirty rows first and
   then wiping and re-pulling from cursor 0 — so the cost of a shorter window is a full resync for a
   device idle longer than it, not lost data. The residual risk it buys down is resurrection: a
   device offline past the window holding a pending edit to a row deleted meanwhile would push that
   edit back. Six weeks is judged sufficient for that.

2. Dead invites are purged 7 days after death, not after the tombstone window. An invite's job ends
   when it is used, revoked or expired; nothing syncs an invite (no change_seq), so purging one
   early cannot affect any client, and the row holds invited_email — a third party's address, for
   someone who may never have become a user. Keep the existing "measure a used invite's age from
   used_at, an unused one from expires_at" rule; only the grace period changes. Give it its own
   constant rather than reusing RETENTION_MS, since the two now mean different things.

Effect on the maintainer's live database, measured from a copy: the tombstoned lists at 72, 66 and
56 days and all the invites that died 58-65 days ago are purged on the first sweep after deploy;
the two tombstones from today stay until day 45. Nothing else changes.
title: Tombstone retention drops to 45 days, and a dead invite is purged 7 days after it dies
